title: Preclinical Cardiac Electrophysiology Assessment by Dual Voltage and Calcium Optical Mapping of Human Organotypic Cardiac Slices
protocol: Prepare 4 L of cardioplegic solution for each heart (composition: 110 mM NaCl, 16 mM KCl, 16 mM MgCl2, 10 mM NaHCO3, 1.2 mM CaCl2; pH = 7.4).
Store 3 L of the cardioplegic solution at 4°C and keep the remaining 1 L at -20°C.

Prepare 1 L each of Tyrode’s slicing solution (composition: 140 mM NaCl, 6 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2, 1.8 mM CaCl2, 10 mM glucose, 10 mM HEPES, 10 mM BDM; pH = 7.4) and Tyrode’s recovery solution (composition: 140 mM NaCl, 4.5 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2, 1.8 mM CaCl2, 10 mM glucose, 10 mM HEPES, 10 mM BDM; pH = 7.4).
Store the slicing and recovery solutions at 4°C until use on the day of the experiment.
Reconstitute RH237 at 1.25 mg/mL in DMSO.
Store RH237 in 30 μL aliquots at 4°C.
Sonicate RH237 using an ultrasound sonicator for at least 10 minutes.
Dilute each RH237 aliquot in 1 mL of recovery solution.
Reconstitute Rhod-2AM at 1 mg/mL in DMSO.
Mix Rhod-2AM with Pluronic F-127 at a 1:1 ratio before dilution.
Store Rhod-2AM in 30 μL aliquots at -20°C.
Dilute each Rhod-2AM aliquot in 1 mL of recovery solution.
Prepare a stock solution of blebbistatin at 2 mg/mL in DMSO.
Store blebbistatin in aliquots at -20°C.
During optical mapping experiments, dilute blebbistatin to a working concentration of 5−10 μM in Tyrode’s recovery solution.
Supplement medium 199 with 2% penicillin-streptomycin and 1x insulin-transferrin-selenium (ITS) liquid media supplement.
Add 10 mM BDM to the supplemented medium.
Filter the culture medium using a 0.2 μm sterile filter.
Store the culture medium at 37°C for use in pharmacological perturbation studies.
Dissolve low-melting point agarose in distilled water.
Heat the mixture in a microwave until fully dissolved.
Cure the agarose in a Petri dish at a thickness of 5 mm and store at 4 °C.
Calibrate the vibrating microtome prior to each experiment.
Load a ceramic cutting blade into the holder and attach the calibrating device provided with the vibrating microtome.
Choose the blade adjustment option from the menu and select ceramic for type of blade.
Select the vibrate option, check for Z axis value.
If this value is <1 μm, exit the calibration menu.
If not, finely adjust the calibration screw attached to the top of the vibrating head and select the vibrate option.
Repeat as many times as needed to set the Z axis to <1 μm.

Set the vibratome settings to 400 μm cutting thickness, 0.02 mm/s advance speed for atrial tissue and 0.04 mm/s advance speed for ventricular tissue, 2 mm horizontal vibration amplitude, and 80 Hz vibration frequency.
Fill the bath of the vibrating microtome with slicing solution at 4 °C.
Maintain the temperature by surrounding the outside of the bath with ice, replenishing as needed throughout the slicing protocol.
Continuously oxygenate the slicing solution in the bath by bubbling with 100% oxygen during slicing.
Set up a second dish with as many 100 μm nylon mesh cell strainers and meshed washers as needed (one cell strainer per slice).
Fill this dish with recovery solution and oxygenate it by bubbling with 100% oxygen at room temperature.
Attach a tissue bath with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) gel layer at the bottom to a perfusion system.
Circulate 1 L of the recovery solution at 37 °C through the perfusion system, maintaining the temperature and clearing accumulation of bath perfusate by oxygenating with 100% oxygen.
Adjust the focus and alignment of the two CMOS cameras using a target.
Use a green LED light source with a wavelength of 520 ± 5 nm to excite the voltage-sensitive and calcium indicator dyes simultaneously.
Prepare a bath of ice-cold cardioplegia by mixing frozen and liquid cardioplegia.
Submerge the heart in the cardioplegia bath until tissue collection for slicing.
Glue premade agarose gel to the back of metal tissue holders of the vibratome.
Identify the left ventricular free wall.
Cut 1 cm³ cubes of tissue in cold cardioplegic solution.
Mount the tissue blocks onto the metal tissue holders with endocardial surfaces facing up and attach them to the agarose gel using topical skin adhesive.
Select a tissue region away from large blood vessels to avoid holes in the slices.
Transfer metal holders into the vibratome bath filled with ice-cold oxygenated slicing solution.
Ensure tissue cubes are completely submerged.
Move blade to front edge of tissue and turn on vibratome.
Discard initial slices until blade reaches smooth endocardial tissue.
Carefully transfer each slice to an oxygenated Tyrode’s recovery solution bath at room temperature.
Place each slice in individual 100 µm nylon mesh cell strainers.
Cover strainers with meshed washers to prevent curling of tissue slices.
Keep slices in the recovery solution for at least 20 minutes.
Sterilize forceps using a bead sterilizer before each transfer step.
Carefully transfer each slice to individual wells of a 6 well plate filled with sterile phosphate-buffered saline.
Gently rock the well plate to rinse slices of recovery solution.
Transfer slices to wells of fresh PBS to thoroughly rinse and sterilize.
Perform wash step 3 times to ensure complete removal of recovery solution from slices.
Transfer slices to individual wells of a 6 well plate filled with 3 mL prewarmed (37 °C) culture medium.
Place plates onto an orbital shaker at 20 rpm in a humidified incubator at 37 °C with 30% O2 and 5% CO2.
Aspirate and replace culture medium every 48 hours.
Transfer the slice of interest to the tissue bath of the perfusion system at 37 °C with 100% O2 in Tyrode’s recovery solution.
Pin down the four corners of the slice to the PDMS gel layer while applying minimal stretch.
Allow slices to rest in this bath with circulating recovery solution for approximately 10 minutes.
Add 0.3−0.5 mL of diluted blebbistatin to the reservoir containing the recovery solution.
Let the slice incubate with blebbistatin for approximately 10 minutes.
Reconstitute 30 µL of the stock voltage-sensitive dye RH237 in 1 mL of recovery solution at 37 °C.
Turn off the pumps and slowly load 0.2−0.3 mL of working dye solution onto the surface of the slice over a period of 30 s.
Allow the slice to incubate in the dye with the pumps off for up to 90 s.
Turn the pumps on again to allow any excess dye to wash out.
Reconstitute the stock calcium indicator Rhod-2AM and load it onto the slice.
Focus the cameras onto the slice by adjusting the distance of the slice from the lens.
Position a bipolar platinum-iridium pacing electrode such that its tip is in contact with the middle of the slice.
Apply pacing stimuli of increasing amplitude to determine the minimum pacing threshold required to elicit an electrical response.
Pace the slice at 1 Hz with a 2 ms pulse width duration at 1.5x the amplitude of the predetermined pacing threshold.
Place a coverslip over the tissue slice.
Illuminate the slice using a 520 ± 5 nm LED excitation light source.
Record the emitted voltage and calcium signals with the two CMOS cameras at 1,000 frames/s.
Check the recording for good signal quality and suppressed motion artifacts.
Add more blebbistatin to the reservoir in steps of 0.1 mL until motion no longer produces artifacts in optical signals.
Add more dye, if needed, to improve signal quality.
Load data files into RHYTHM1.2 by selecting any one of the four display windows on the screen and using the Select Directory and Load buttons.
Select Camera 1 for voltage signal loading.
Repeat process to load calcium signal (Camera 2) to an adjacent display window.
Select Dual Data Linking checkbox between the two selected display windows to link the two data sets.
Select Data Analysis | Condition Parameters to condition the voltage and calcium optical mapping data prior to further analysis.
Remove background pixels based on fluorescent intensity threshold using the “Remove Background” function.
Perform spatial averaging of the optical mapping data using the “Bin” function.
Filter the optical mapping data using a band pass filter with the “Filter” function.
Use the “Drift” function to remove baseline drift in the optical mapping signal.
Normalize the optical mapping data from each pixel to have a maximal amplitude of 1 using the “Normalize” function.
Invert calcium traces for further analysis using the “Inverse Signal” function.
Select conditioned trace from any given spot and plot it in the Waveform window using Display Wave.
Adjust signal conditioning parameters to obtain optimal action potential and calcium transient traces.
